text: Writing clean code is a skill that every developer should practice. The main goal is to make your code readable for other people, not just for the computer. One of the first steps is to use clear and consistent naming conventions. For example, a variable called `totalPrice` is much easier to understand than `tp`. The same rule applies to functions: their names should describe what they do, like `calculateDiscount()` instead of `doStuff()`. Keeping functions short and focused on a single task also helps a lot. When every function has one clear purpose, you can test and reuse it easily. All these habits improve maintainability, meaning that future changes become simpler and less risky, saving time and frustration in the long run.
